estimate: Cosmetic-only pass (dirs, sample plugin, docs, i18n, bundled-tree rename + hash regen): roughly half a day plus a bundled-hash helper script. Full contract rename with accept-both shims for the manifest filename, `engines` key, and the four panel wire strings, including the atomic frame-name/placeholder change and updated e2e containment fixtures: 2-3 days, with the bundled `contentHash` regeneration and the consent-refingerprinting fallout as the two items most likely to slip.
gotchas: `src/relay/plugin-overlay.ts` and the `hook-plugin-*.ts` files under `src/main/opencode/` match a `plugin` grep and are full of `orca` literals (`.orca-relay`, `orca-opencode-status.js`, `@orca-managed-pi-extension`), but they belong to the agent-status overlay system, not the plugin system. Touching them in a plugin-surface change breaks SSH agent status.

Of the ~138 `orca` literals inside plugin-named files, the heaviest concentrations are tests and fixtures (`plugin-install.test.ts`: 53, `skill-plugin-cache-scan.test.ts`: 121). Raw grep counts wildly overstate the production surface — the real contract is about six constants in three shared files.

`PLUGIN_HOST_API_V0` is the single source of truth for three things at once: the capability gate, the panel-callable action allowlist (`PLUGIN_PANEL_ACTIONS` is derived by filtering `panel: true`), and the worker SDK. Adding or renaming a method there changes what sandboxed panels may call, which is easy to do accidentally.

`readPanelPongId` is a hand-rolled mirror of `panelPongSchema`, written that way because a failed zod parse allocates an issue list (~90x the accept path) and a hostile panel can spam near-miss pongs. Replacing it with `safeParse` for tidiness reintroduces a DoS vector.

The panel shell prepends the CSP `<meta>` before any plugin markup, and `fillPanelShell` uses first-occurrence `String.replace`. That ordering is what makes a plugin echoing the placeholder string inert — switching to `replaceAll` or moving the fill after plugin content would let a plugin inject its own tokens.

The renderer keys the panel iframe on `${tabKey}:${documentRevision}:${themeRevision}`, and `right-sidebar-panel-content.tsx` also keys `<PluginPanel key={effectiveTab}>`. Both are deliberate: a reused frame could keep posting messages while the bridge is rebound under the next plugin's identity. Dropping either key looks like a harmless remount optimization and creates a cross-plugin authority bug.

`resolvePluginPanelIcon` uses `Object.hasOwn` so a manifest icon named `constructor` cannot resolve to an inherited member and crash the sidebar. The same defensive pattern appears in storage keys (`RESERVED_STORAGE_KEYS`), plugin ids (`DANGEROUS_PLUGIN_NAMES`), and `isTopLevelView` — treat prototype-key rejection as a house invariant, not local paranoia.

There is a `generate:bundled-skill-guides` and a `generate:skill-bundle-manifest` script but no bundled-plugin equivalent, so the `contentHash` in `bundled-plugins.json` has to be regenerated by hand or by a new script. It is the one place in this change with no CI safety net until bootstrap fails at runtime.

AGENTS.md bans `max-lines` disables outright and `config/max-lines-baseline.txt` may only shrink, yet several files you must edit are near their budget (`right-sidebar/index.tsx` already carries a grandfathered disable at 543 lines). Plan for a split, not a suppression.

`plugin-error-presentation.ts` matches error text by substring (`detail.includes('orca-plugin.json')`). Renaming the manifest filename without updating that matcher degrades every install failure to the generic message, which reads as a UX regression rather than a missed rename.

orderedSteps: Decide the compatibility posture before touching anything: (a) cosmetic-only rename of dir names / sample plugin / docs / i18n, or (b) contract rename of `orca-plugin.json`, `engines.orca`, and the four `orca-panel-*` wire strings. Option (b) breaks every already-installed and marketplace-published plugin unless dual-read shims ship first.

Baseline the gates so later failures are attributable: `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm exec vitest run --config config/vitest.config.ts src/shared/plugins src/main/plugins src/renderer/src/components/right-sidebar src/renderer/src/store/plugin-panels.test.ts src/main/ipc/plugins.test.ts`.

Shared contract first, since main and renderer both import it. In `plugin-manifest.ts` introduce the new manifest filename as primary and keep `orca-plugin.json` as a read fallback in `readPluginManifestText`/`plugin-manifest-file.ts`; accept both `engines.orca` and the new key in the schema (union, not replace) so `satisfiesOrcaEngineRange` still gates old manifests.

Panel wire protocol: in `plugin-panel-bridge.ts` add the new type strings and make `looksLikePanelActionRequest`, `parsePanelActionRequest`, and `readPanelPongId` accept old and new. Emit only the new strings from the host (`plugin-panel-shell.ts` prelude, renderer ping) so new panels are clean while old panels keep working.

Frame-name prefix and shell placeholders must change in one commit across three files: `plugin-panel-bridge.ts` (constant), `src/main/plugins/plugin-panel-navigation-guard.ts` (registry match), and `src/renderer/src/components/right-sidebar/PluginPanel.tsx` (iframe `name` + `fillPanelShell`). A partial change fails open on containment or silently drops design tokens.

Marketplace identity: update `PLUGIN_MARKETPLACE_FILENAME`, `OFFICIAL_PLUGIN_ID_PREFIX`, `OFFICIAL_MARKETPLACE_REPOSITORY`, and the default source URL in `plugin-marketplace.ts`; confirm `isOfficialPluginIdentity` still accepts every key in `resources/plugins/launch/orca-marketplace.json` and `bundled-plugins.json`.

Rename the three bundled plugin trees under `resources/plugins/launch/` plus their `orca-plugin.json` files, then recompute `contentHash` with `hashPluginTree` from `src/main/plugins/plugin-content-hash.ts` and write the new value into `bundled-plugins.json`. There is no `generate:bundled-plugins` npm script — script this or bootstrap will reject the tree at startup.
Rename the `examples/plugins/hello-orca` sample (dir, manifest id, publisher, panel copy) and update `examples/plugins/hostile-panel/panel.html` message types in lockstep with step 4.

Renderer copy and error matching: update `src/renderer/src/components/settings/plugin-error-presentation.ts` (it substring-matches `orca-plugin.json`) and `PluginInstallDialog.tsx` help text, then run `pnpm sync:localization-catalog` and verify with `pnpm verify:localization-catalog && pnpm verify:localization-coverage`.

Update the four e2e specs (`plugin-demo`, `plugin-panel-containment`, `plugin-marketplace-content`, `plugin-startup-budget`) and `tests/e2e/helpers/plugin-panel-navigation-observer.ts` to the new tokens; add a regression test that an old-token manifest and an old-token panel message still work, so the compat shims are pinned rather than incidental.

Re-run the gates plus the plugin e2e project, and separately exercise the subsystem with `settings.pluginSystemEnabled` flipped on (it defaults false, so nothing below the settings toggle runs otherwise): install the sample from a local path, consent, open the panel, invoke the worker command, then confirm containment probes still report CONTAINED.

Finish with `pnpm run check:max-lines-ratchet` and `pnpm run check:reliability-gates`; if any touched file crossed its budget, split it rather than adding a disable (AGENTS.md forbids max-lines disables outright).
risks: Renaming `orca-plugin.json` or `engines.orca` without a read fallback fails manifest parsing wholesale — every installed plugin, every marketplace listing, and the three bundled packs become `invalid` at once, and the failure surfaces as a generic settings-row error rather than a migration prompt.

Changing the four `orca-panel-*` postMessage strings is a silent break for third-party panels: the host deliberately ignores messages whose `type` it does not recognize (`looksLikePanelActionRequest`), so an old panel simply stops working with no error anywhere.

`PLUGIN_PANEL_FRAME_NAME_PREFIX` is a security boundary, not a label. The main-process navigation registry binds frames by that name at `frame-created`, before plugin script can mutate `window.name`. If the renderer's iframe `name` and the guard's prefix diverge, navigation containment fails open while every happy-path test still passes.

Any byte change inside a bundled plugin tree invalidates the pinned `contentHash` in `bundled-plugins.json`; bootstrap rejects the mismatch and the bundled navigation-shortcuts pack disappears silently on a fresh profile.

Content-hash changes also flow into `canonicalizePluginConsent` for instructional packs (keybindings/vmRecipes/agents), so renaming files inside those trees re-prompts consent for existing users and leaves their panels disabled until they re-approve.

The persisted right-sidebar route stores `plugin:<publisher>.<id>/<panelId>`. Rebranding publisher/id strings orphans those keys, and `normalizeRightSidebarRoute` resets unknown-shaped keys to Explorer without telling the user their pinned panel is gone.

Localization is CI-gated in both directions: `verify:localization-catalog` (key/placeholder parity across en/es/ja/ko/zh) and `verify:localization-coverage` (allowlist of unlocalized renderer strings). Editing plugin settings copy without running the sync script fails PR checks even though the code is correct.
The subsystem ships off (`pluginSystemEnabled: false`), so a regression can pass a full manual smoke test and land unnoticed; verification must explicitly enable the flag.
summary: The plugin system is large but well-layered: 41 files in `src/shared/plugins` hold the Electron-free contract (manifest schema, capability set, host-API spec table, panel bridge/shell), 108 files in `src/main/plugins` hold discovery/install/consent/worker/panel enforcement, and the renderer consumes it through `store/plugin-panels.ts`, `right-sidebar/PluginPanel.tsx`, and ~29 `settings/Plugin*.tsx` files. 264 files repo-wide carry a `plugin` name; only ~138 `orca` literals live inside them and most are in tests. The brand tokens that actually matter are few and load-bearing: the manifest filename `orca-plugin.json`, the `engines.orca` range key, the marketplace filename/official prefix (`orca-marketplace.json`, `orca-`, repo `orca-plugins`), the four postMessage type strings `orca-panel-action|-result|-ping|-pong`, the iframe name prefix `orca-plugin-panel:`, and the shell placeholders `__ORCA_COLOR_SCHEME__` / `/*__ORCA_PANEL_TOKENS__*/`. Three of those are live wire/security contracts shared with third-party plugin trees, so they need accept-both compatibility rather than a straight find-and-replace. The rest (dir names, sample plugin, docs, i18n strings) are cosmetic but gated by CI ratchets: localization catalog parity across 5 locales, the max-lines baseline (may only shrink), and the pinned `contentHash` in `resources/plugins/launch/bundled-plugins.json`.
surface: Orca's plugin subsystem end to end — manifest contract → discovery/install → consent → out-of-process worker + sandboxed panel bridge → marketplace/bundled content — and every `orca`-brand token embedded in that surface (filenames, wire strings, official-identity prefixes, bundled plugin keys, examples, i18n copy).
